scope: Experimental browser-service bundles. No tracked production runtime changes, full-API integration or new 100-target result in this experiment.
conclusion: Contained WebKit is a candidate for opt-in integration: five of five matched Saks visits retrieved the expected rendered product content, versus zero of five for each existing engine. The earlier 16-target engine comparison was tied at three successes per engine. A default-UA WebKit visit succeeded at Saks in the UA experiment, motivating the matched replication. This selected-site result does not establish aggregate coverage or hosted parity.

requestAccounting.ancillaryRequests: Separate geolocation checks and one Node TLS diagnostic are not benchmark RPCs. All guard/RTC/TLS fixtures were locally owned; native macOS WebKit visited no public benchmark targets.

method.saksReplication: Five independent fresh-context visits per engine, rotating engine order, a fifteen-second wait before each matched batch, GitHub controls before and after. Deliberate measurements are not automatic retries.

networkBoundary.requiredLocalSsrfFilter: Local filtering proxy validates target destinations and DNS; it does not provide upstream egress rotation.
networkBoundary.experimentalWebkit: Trusted root service with NET_ADMIN confined to its owned container namespace. Browser drops to UID 1000, effective capabilities zero and NoNewPrivs=1. Container-local IPv4/IPv6 UID policy permits only TCP to the local filter port; the browser cannot configure those rules.
networkBoundary.limits: The owned test exercised IPv4 transports; an IPv6 reject rule was installed but no actual IPv6 packet negative test is claimed. The native macOS sandbox wrapper failed owned loopback/RTC containment and was not used for public targets. An earlier WebSocket proxy-hop assertion was inconclusive, not evidence of a private endpoint leak. Least-privilege deployment and child-environment isolation still require production design and tests.

tlsRepair.initialControl: The initial three GitHub control calls stopped the run: Chromium and Firefox passed; WebKit rejected the certificate. The system CA bundle was absent.
tlsRepair.repair: Installed the standard ca-certificates package. TLS verification remains enabled; no ignoreHTTPSErrors bypass.

Chromium/Firefox keep their existing policies; experimental WebKit uses a separate browser UID with container-local network filtering, a root trusted service and NET_ADMIN in that owned namespace. Page scripts stay enabled. This is a selected-target browser-service experiment, not a full API result or a production deployment.

saksReplication.scope: Matched Chromium/Firefox/contained-WebKit replication of the single Saks recovery. Five independent fresh-context visits to Saks and a GitHub control before and after, per engine; fifteen-second between-batch wait before Saks, seven-second per-profile minimum pacing, three HTTP workers and no client retries. Source, image, TLS verification and containment match the preceding browser-service experiment. Repeated visits are deliberate measurement rounds, not automatic request retries. Not a full API or 100-target result.

comparisonLimits: Browser-service experiments are not full Firecrawl API runs.
Only sixteen selected targets plus matched Saks replication; no extrapolation to the frozen hundred.
Time, rate effects, shared host load, browser identity and engine-specific containment remain confounders. The engine bundles differ in more than one variable.

The configured seven-second pacer reserves a slot before fetch. Minimum observed gaps by profile were 6991-7001 ms; it is not a verified exact seven-second dispatch floor. Raw deviations are retained.
UA/platform edits did not establish an improvement. Default WebKit UA describes macOS while the runtime platform is Linux; the Linux and pinned-upstream GLib formats each scored three of sixteen.
No hosted calls were made. The last full100 primary/fallback scores remain 46/56; the historical hosted reference remains 82 and was not refreshed.
integrationPending: Explicit WebKit engine configuration and launch-port plumbing in the production service.
A deployment network boundary that preserves SSRF/RTC containment, isolates browser child environment and limits trusted privileges.
Full API routing, fallback/session compatibility, focused happy/failure tests, then a bounded proxy-free hundred-target evaluation.

sourceResearch.finding: Playwright WebKit is a patched upstream build, not installed Safari.
Pinned upstream GLib format uses uname platform and Version/60.5. This is not proof of Playwright default UA.
Build options alone cannot establish the installed binary RTC behavior; owned transport probes measured it.
